john_m (Acme Mobile): Hey team — started seeing 401 invalid_api_key from our iOS app since yesterday. Backend request-id=req_9f4a. We didn't rotate keys. curl from my laptop using the same key works. Any ideas?

lina_support: thanks — can you paste the raw request headers from a failing device (redact the key) and the SDK/version you’re running?

john_m (Acme Mobile): headers from device (redacted):
```
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: ApiKey sk_live_abc123REDACT
User-Agent: MyApp/3.2.1 (iPhone)
```
Using Alamofire 5.6.2 and our in-house auth helper that attaches auth header.

dev_jordan: quick note — our ingestion checks the Authorization scheme. We accept either: `Authorization: Bearer <KEY>` or `x-api-key: <KEY>`; if the scheme is anything else (e.g. `ApiKey`) it treats it as an unsupported token and returns 401. Curl working is consistent because you used `Authorization: Bearer ...` there.

john_m (Acme Mobile): aha — our helper was formatting `Authorization: ApiKey <val>` (was trying to be explicit). We'll change it to `Authorization: Bearer <val>` and redeploy a patch to a small canary.

john_m (Acme Mobile): quick follow-up — patched header, canary shows success, no more 401s for the same request-id pattern.

lina_support: perfect. I'll add a short KB entry: "Clients must use `Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>` or the `x-api-key` header; other schemes (ApiKey, Token, etc.) are not recognized and will result in 401 invalid_api_key." Closing the thread unless you want us to keep monitoring :thumbsup:

ticket-bot: Created support ticket #SUP-2024-5921 for tracking and KB sync.
